subject: Re: Post-call: Performance SLO / SLA follow-up (latency, throughput, streaming)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acme.com>, Bryan Lee <bryan.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 8 Oct 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + next steps: Performance targets and SLA language

Thanks again for taking the call today — great to meet the Acme team. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can sync on SLOs/SLA language before legal/procurement gets involved.

Summary of what we discussed:
- Target latency: p95 <= 350ms for text-generation (single-turn, up to 1024 tokens).
- Throughput: baseline 200 requests/sec, burst to 500 rps for 5 min windows.
- Concurrency: support for 100 concurrent streams (long-poll streaming use case).
- Streaming: response chunking acceptable; developer expects start-of-response within 100ms p50 for streaming-enabled requests.
- Measurement: Redwood measures latency from request arrival at edge to last token emitted by renderer (details below).

Open clarifications we agreed to confirm:
1) Exact definition of "latency" to include/exclude customer-side network and client-side rendering. We propose: latency measured at Redwood ingress to egress (server-side only).
2) Maintenance and force majeure exclusions: typical 4-hr maintenance window per month and planned maintenance with 48-hr notice.
3) Reporting cadence: monthly availability & latency report via Console + CSV export; incident reports for incidents exceeding 1% error rate.
4) Remedies: service credits starting at SLA violation threshold (e.g., >1% of requests above p95 target in a billing month).

Next steps / asks:
- Acme: confirm that the proposed p95/p50 targets and throughput/streaming expectations align with product needs.
- Redwood: share a short SLA draft and an example SLO measurement spec (attached).
- Schedule: propose we agree by EOD Monday so we can include language in the MSA/quote.

Attachments: Redwood_SLA_Draft_v1.pdf (draft SLA language), acme_mutual-action-plan.xlsx (timeline + owners).

Thanks — I can jump on another call if you want to walk through the SLA line-by-line.
\Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0124

From: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acme.com>

Date: Fri, 9 Oct 2026 09:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps: Performance targets and SLA language

Thanks Marissa — helpful recap. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

- Measurement: we prefer latency measured end-to-end from our client to final token, but understand Redwood's measurement model. Can you confirm the ingress->egress definition and whether we can request a customer-facing measurement that includes our network?
- Streaming: the key requirement is start-of-response within 100ms for p50 for streaming calls; total completion can be longer since responses are streaming. Also need guidance on the max idle time per stream before Redwood tears down an idle connection.
- Throughput: the 200 rps baseline is fine; what does burst look like from a provisioning perspective (how quickly can you scale from 200 -> 500 rps)?

We'll review the SLA draft and get back with redlines. Also looping in our infra lead (Bryan) for the concurrency/idle-time question.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acme.com>, Bryan Lee <bryan.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 9 Oct 2026 12:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps: Performance targets and SLA language

Alice — thanks for the quick reply and the helpful questions. Short answers below, and I attached a one-pager measurement spec in the SLA draft for legal.

1) Measurement definition:
- Redwood's standard measurement is server-side: time between request arrival at Redwood edge (timestamped at our ingress load balancer) and the time when the last token for that request is emitted by Redwood's renderer. This excludes client/network latency.
- For customers who need end-to-end metrics, we support a lightweight client SDK ping and synthetic checks that can be included in the Console reports; those can be used by Acme as an independent measurement. We can coordinate instrumentation with your infra team.

2) Streaming idle timeout and start-of-response:
- Start-of-response: we can guarantee p50 <= 100ms for start-of-response for streaming-enabled requests under normal operating load (the same request sizing constraints as discussed: <=1024 tokens).
- Idle timeout: default 60s idle before idle connection termination; can extend to 5 minutes for a configuration/contracted option.

3) Burst scaling and provisioning:
- Autoscaler can provision additional inference capacity within ~90s for typical model families. For guaranteed burst-to-500 rps with no cold-start risk, we recommend a reserved buffer (Dedicated slot reservation) — we outlined options in the Mutual Action Plan attachment.

4) SLA language (high-level):
- Measurement window: monthly; p95 latency target as agreed; exclusions include scheduled maintenance (>=48hr notice), force majeure, and customer misconfiguration.
- Remedies: service credit tiers starting at 5% credit for minor violations (monthly p95 breach >1% of requests) scaling to larger credits for broader availability impacts.
- Reporting: monthly CSV + Console dashboard + post-incident report within 72 hours for Sev1 incidents.

Next steps:
- Bryan: can you confirm whether Acme wants client-side synthetic checks included in the official monthly report (we can include both server and client measurements side-by-side)?
- Acme legal/procurement: we'll accept reasonable redlines but would like to avoid changes that require redefining measurement points.

If helpful, Rishi and I can join a short technical call with Bryan next week to walk through the measurement and instrumentation options. 

Thanks,
Marissa

Subject: Fwd: Post-call: Performance SLO / SLA follow-up (latency, throughput, streaming)

Looping in Neha for FYI — couple notes before we send the updated SLA to Acme: 

- Pricing implication: guaranteeing extended idle-time and reserved burst capacity will add to the committed capacity cost. We should include two options in the quote: (A) Standard hosted SLA (server-side measurement, 60s idle default, autoscaler) and (B) Enterprise SLA (5min idle, reserved burst to 500 rps, enhanced reporting).
- Legal ask: keep measurement point as ingress->egress. If Acme insists on customer-facing measurement being the canonical metric, it opens procurement complexity.
- Action: Marissa, please send the updated Redwood_SLA_Draft_v1.pdf with the specific credit schedule and option callouts; I'll draft pricing delta bullets for procurement.

Thanks,
Rishi
